title: Aeneas Carries Anchises from Troy
text:
On the night Troy fell, the Greeks poured out of the wooden horse and the city was burning. The Trojan prince Aeneas fought until he saw it was hopeless. His mother, the goddess Venus, showed him the gods themselves tearing down the walls, and told him to go home and save his family.

But at home his old father Anchises refused to leave. He would not outlive Troy, he said. Aeneas, desperate, prepared to go back and die fighting rather than abandon him. Then a soft flame appeared around the head of his little son Ascanius, flickering harmlessly in his hair. Anchises asked Jupiter for a confirming sign; there was a crack of thunder and a shooting star blazed over the city. The old man gave way.

Aeneas told his father to climb on his shoulders and to carry the household gods, since his own hands were stained with blood. He took his son by the hand, and his wife Creusa followed behind. They hurried through the dark, burning streets.

At the meeting place outside the city, Creusa was missing. Aeneas ran back through the ruins calling her name. Her ghost appeared to him, told him that the gods had other plans for her, and asked him to love their son. He tried three times to embrace her, and three times his arms closed on air. He returned and led the survivors to the mountains.
lesson: In a crisis, a family is carried on shoulders and led by the hand. Care for the old and the young together, even when it slows you down.
location: Troy (modern Turkey, myth); written in Rome, Italy
